# Batwing — Copilot Instructions

These are the Batwing invariants: the small set of facts that are true in every
repository in the `batwingatx` organization and that change almost never. The
full, evolving rule set lives in one place — see **Full rules** at the bottom.

## Organization

- The canonical GitHub organization is **`batwingatx`**. All Batwing work lives there.
- Never create or push a Batwing repository under the personal account `nickarthur`.
- `batwing-studios` is **retired** and returns HTTP 404. Never write to it, and never
  cite it as the canonical organization.

## Product names — authoritative

- **BATS** is the *Basic Airmanship Training System* — an umbrella training system,
  not a single application. Never expand it as "BAT Studio" or
  "Batwing Aviation Training Suite".
- SKUs: **BATS Engine** (training runtime), **BATS Studio** (authoring),
  **BATS View** (document viewer), **BATS Explorer** (scenic companion),
  **BATS Cam** (cinematic camera), **BATS Check** (voice checklists),
  **BATS Voice** (voice packs).
- Deliberately outside the BATS prefix: **Bat Bridge** (MSFS integration layer) and
  **NavBat** (marine navigation console).
- **Retired names — never use:** `BAT` as a standalone product, `Bat View`, `Bat Cam`,
  `Bat Voice`, `Bat Check`, `Bat Explorer`, `Batwing Explorer`, `Batwing Studios`.

## Naming and versioning

- **No version suffixes in filenames.** Versioning happens through Git tags and
  `CHANGELOG.md`. Never create `SKILL-v1.md` or `foo-v0.2.md`. An identifier like
  `ADR-BW-001` is a sequence number, not a version suffix, and is exempt.
- **One canonical file per concept.** Do not duplicate a rule across files. If two
  places need the same rule, one of them links to the other.
- Documentation that restates rules owned by another file is a pointer, not a copy.

## Provenance

- A commit that originates from an agent thread ends its message with a
  `Perplexity Origin Thread:` footer naming that thread. Provenance is not optional;
  it is how a future reader reconstructs why a change exists.
- Prefer small, explicit, easy-to-diff changes over large rewrites.

## Autonomy — who decides what

- **In the editor, with a human present:** make reversible, in-scope changes and report
  them. Do not ask permission for reversible work; explaining what you did is not the
  same as asking whether you may.
- **Unattended (cloud/coding agent):** open a pull request. Never push directly to
  `main`. Merge gating is branch protection's job — do not ask a human to approve
  something a rule already enforces.
- **Always escalate, regardless of surface:** anything irreversible (force-push, history
  rewrite, deletion, permission or protection changes), anything that writes to an
  external system (Jira, Confluence, releases, tags), and any case where two
  authoritative documents disagree. Surface the conflict instead of guessing.

## Full rules

The evolving rule set is **not** duplicated here. Read it at
<https://github.com/batwingatx/batwing-agents>:

- `skills/ops-bat/SKILL.md` — operations, Jira/Confluence, thread lifecycle, provenance
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — the Copilot-facing rules for that repo
- `CHANGELOG.md` — what changed, when, and which thread originated it
